Actually grep -b prints byte offset, but maybe the file is larger, but wc shows only 1487 lines. So the grep output line numbers might be from a different version or something. Something weird: maybe the repository is large and wc shows only line count of something else? Let's check file size: maybe there are many lines but wc -l only counts lines terminated by newline; maybe there are very long lines? But 44087 byte offset could be beyond file size. Something is inconsistent. Let's just read the file to see its content. Possibly the file is large (maybe it's compiled python?). But wc -l says 1487 lines, which is relatively small. So grep -b gave bogus large line numbers because maybe there were binary matches? Or maybe the file is not parse.py but some other file? Actually the grep command was "grep -b 'class Result(object):' parse.py". That should search within parse.py for that text. It returned "44087:class Result(object):". That suggests the match is at byte offset 44087, but the file only has 1487 lines; maybe each line is long and the offset is in bytes, not line numbers. So the file could be larger (maybe many lines but wc -l only counts lines that end with newline; maybe some lines are very long and there are less newline characters?). But 44087 bytes is plausible if file is ~44KB. So wc -l only counted 1487 lines because many lines may not end with newline? That seems odd. Let's get file size: use stat -c%s parse.py.
